s.dp: Communication › Boast
s.d: to express an unusually high degree of confidence in someone or something being exceptionally noteworthy{N:001}
s.c: Whether in any particular context the boasting is legitimate or not depends upon what is boasted about. In a number of languages, however, quite different terms are employed, depending upon the differing degrees of justification for such boasting.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to move to or toward a reference point of the viewpoint character or event{N:001}

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (an Aramaic word)
s.c: The expression μαρανα θα in ⟦1 Corinthians 16:22|1 Corinthians 16:22⟧ is an Aramaic formula evidently associated with early Christian liturgy. It must have been widely used, since it occurs in ⟦1 Corinthians 16:22|1 Corinthians 16:22⟧ without explanation.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: (an Aramaic word) to move to or toward a reference point of the viewpoint character or event{N:001}

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: to be a follower or a disciple of someone, in the sense of adhering to the teachings or instructions of a leader and in promoting the cause of such a leader
s.g: to follow; to be a disciple of
s.c: Though many translators have attempted to employ the metaphorical significance of ‘to follow’ in the sense of ‘to be a disciple of,’ there are certain dangers in a number of languages. For example, ‘to follow’ may often have the connotation of ‘to pursue after with evil intent.’ In many languages the appropriate equivalent of ‘to follow’ (in the sense of ‘to be a disciple’) is literally ‘to accompany’ or ‘to go along with’ or ‘to be in the group of.’

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: to cause someone to become a disciple or follower of
s.g: to make disciples; to cause people to become followers
s.c: In rendering μαθητεύω in ⟦Matthew 28:19|Matthew 28:19⟧ and similar contexts, it is important to avoid the implication of duress or force, that is to say, one should not translate ‘force them to be my disciples’ or ‘compel them to be my disciples.’ This might very well be implied in a literal translation of a causative such as ‘to make.’ In order to avoid a wrong implication of a causative, it may be important to use some such expression as ‘convince them to become my disciples’ or ‘urge them to be my disciples.’

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: (derivative of {L:μαθητεύω<SDBG:μαθητεύω:000000>}[a] ‘to follow, to be a disciple of,’ {D:36.31}) a person who is a disciple or follower of someone
s.c: Though in the NT μαθητής generally refers to men, it is neutral as to sex distinction, and thus in a few instances in the NT also includes women (as in ⟦Acts 6:1|Acts 6:1⟧, πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ‘the number of disciples kept growing’). In some languages it may be important to indicate clearly the sex distinction, and in those contexts in which the twelve disciples are being referred to, obviously the reference must be to men. However, when the wider group of disciples is referred to, then some indication should be introduced as to the fact that both men and women were involved.

s.dp: Learn
s.d: (derivative of {L:μανθάνω<SDBG:μανθάνω:000000>}[a] ‘to learn, to be instructed,’ {D:27.12}) a person who learns from another by instruction, whether formal or informal{N:001}

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: (derivative of {L:μαθητεύω<SDBG:μαθητεύω:000000>}[a] ‘to follow, to be a disciple of,’ {D:36.31}) a disciple who is a woman

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: to regard someone as happy or fortunate in view of favorable circumstances
s.g: to regard as happy; to regard as fortunate

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: pertaining to being happy, with the implication of enjoying favorable circumstances
s.c: The passive construction in ⟦Matthew 5:7|Matthew 5:7⟧ (ἐλεηθήσονται) is generally regarded as a so-called ‘passive of avoidance,’ that is to say, the use of a passive form in order to avoid a direct reference to God.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Happy, Glad, Joyful
s.d: a state of happiness, implying favorable circumstances
s.c: In ⟦Galatians 4:15|Galatians 4:15⟧ μακαρισμός clearly refers to a state of happiness which occurred in the past but which was no longer evident. It may therefore be necessary to indicate that the happiness in question is past, and accordingly, one may translate ‘you were so happy! What has happened?’ or ‘then you were so happy! What has happened to you now?’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a Roman province in Greece

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of {L:Μακεδονία<SDBG:Μακεδονία:000000>} ‘Macedonia,’ {D:93.527}) a person who is a native of Macedonia

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Earn, Gain, Do Business
s.d: an area in a city or town where meat was sold
s.c: Μάκελλον would normally be a particular part of the ἀγορά (LN 57.207).

s.dp: Spacial Positions › At, Beside, Near, Far
s.d: a position at a relatively great distance from another position{N:001}
s.g: far; at a distance; some distance away; far away
s.c: For εἰς in ⟦Acts 2:39|Acts 2:39⟧, see LN 84.16).

s.dp: Spacial Positions › At, Beside, Near, Far
s.d: a position at a relatively great distance from another position{N:001}
s.g: far; at a distance; some distance away; far away

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Patience, Endurance, Perseverance
s.d: (derivative of {L:μακροθυμία<SDBG:μακροθυμία:000000>} ‘patience,’ {D:25.167}) to demonstrate patience despite difficulties
s.g: to be patient; to remain patient; to wait patiently

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: to extend a period of time on the basis of a particular mental attitude
s.g: to be slow to; to delay in

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Patience, Endurance, Perseverance
s.d: a state of emotional calm in the face of provocation or misfortune and without complaint or irritation
s.c: In a number of languages ‘patience’ is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to remain seated in one’s heart’ or ‘to keep one’s heart from jumping’ or ‘to have a waiting heart.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Patience, Endurance, Perseverance
s.d: (derivative of {L:μακροθυμία<SDBG:μακροθυμία:000000>} ‘patience,’ {D:25.167}) pertaining to being patient
s.c: In ⟦Acts 26:3|Acts 26:3⟧ it may be necessary in some languages to spell out the implications of μακροθύμως, for example, ‘therefore I beg you to listen to me without interrupting’ or ‘… without stopping me.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a relatively long duration of time
s.g: long; long time; for some time

s.dp: Spacial Dimensions › Long, Short, Far
s.d: pertaining to being far from some point of reference

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a relatively long duration of time
s.g: long; long time; for some time

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: a state of weakness resulting from disease{N:001}

s.dp: Features of Objects › Soft, Tender
s.d: pertaining to being soft to the touch

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sexual Misbehavior
s.d: the passive male partner in homosexual intercourse
s.c: For a context of μαλακός, see ⟦1 Corinthians 6:9|1 Corinthians 6:9⟧ in LN 88.280. As in Greek, a number of other languages also have entirely distinct terms for the active and passive roles in homosexual intercourse.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.d: a very high point on a scale of extent{N:001}

s.dp: Degree › More Than, Less Than [Comparative Degree]
s.d: a degree which surpasses in some manner a point on an explicit or implicit scale of extent
s.g: more; more than; to a greater degree; even more

s.dp: Relations › Contrast
s.d: a marker of contrast indicating an alternative
s.g: on the contrary; instead; but rather

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the high priests slave whom Peter wounded

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: the mother of one’s own mother or father (with a possible connotation of affection)
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to distinguish between the grandmother on one’s father’s side and the grandmother on one’s mother’s side. There is no positive indication in ⟦2 Timothy 1:5|2 Timothy 1:5⟧ as to the particular relationship involved, but one may assume that the grandmother Lois was the mother of Eunice, and therefore it would be the grandmother on the mother’s side.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Be Rich, Be Wealthy
s.d: wealth and riches, with a strongly negative connotation

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a son of Ἰωσήφ[a] and ancestor of an Israelite tribe

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Learn
s.d: to acquire information as the result of instruction, whether in an informal or formal context
s.g: to learn; to be instructed; to be taught

s.dp: Learn
s.d: to learn from experience, often with the implication of reflection
s.g: to learn; to come to realize

s.dp: Understand › Come To Understand
s.d: to come to understand as the result of a process of learning
s.c: It is possible to understand μανθάνω in ⟦1 Corinthians 4:6|1 Corinthians 4:6⟧ as meaning simply ‘to learn’ (see LN 27.12).

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to think or reason in a completely irrational manner{N:001}
s.g: to not be in one’s right mind; to be insane; to be mad; to be out of one’s mind; insanity; madness
s.c: In some languages μανία is best rendered by an idiomatic expression, for example, ‘thoughts that never return,’ ‘distorted thoughts,’ ‘senseless thoughts,’ or ‘thoughts that cannot be understood.’

s.dp: Foods and Condiments › Food
s.d: the miraculous food given by God to the Israelites during their journey through the wilderness
s.c: In most languages μάννα is rendered by a transliteration as ‘manna’ or ‘mana.’ One must, however, be very careful about the transliteration of this term, since it may correspond to an indigenous expression having quite a different meaning. Although in the OT it may be useful to have a marginal note explaining the play on words involved in the derivation of this term, in the NT one can usually use an expression such as ‘food called manna.’

s.dp: Communication › Foretell, Tell Fortunes
s.d: to function as a more or less professional predicter of future events for the sake of a fee
s.c: In ⟦Acts 16:16|Acts 16:16⟧ μαντεύομαι may often be translated as ‘for money she told people what was going to happen to them.’

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to go out of existence gradually
s.c: In many languages it is simply not possible to speak of a ‘rich man fading away.’ Colors may fade, but not a person, and therefore it may be necessary to shift the figure of speech, for example, ‘the rich man will end up being no one’ or ‘the rich man will finally count for nothing.’

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: a smooth, rounded concretion formed within the shells of certain mollusks and valued as a gem because of its lustrous color (see {D:2.29})
s.c: In general there is little difficulty involved in obtaining a satisfactory term for ‘pearl,’ since such objects are relatively well known throughout the world. However, in some languages there is no term for ‘pearl,’ and therefore one may use in the case of ⟦Revelation 21:21|Revelation 21:21⟧ ‘beautiful white stones,’ and in ⟦Matthew 7:6|Matthew 7:6⟧ it may be appropriate to translate ‘do not throw your valuable jewels to pigs.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a sister of {L:Mary<SDBG:Μαρία:000001>}[b] and {L:Lazarus<SDBG:Λάζαρος:000000>}[a] of Bethany

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a sister of {L:Martha<SDBG:Μάρθα:000000>} and {L:Lazarus<SDBG:Λάζαρος:000000>}[a]

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the mother of {L:James<SDBG:Ἰάκωβος:000003>}[d] and {L:Joseph<SDBG:Ἰωσήφ:000006>}[g]

s.d: a person greeted in {S:04501600600004}

s.d: a companion of Paul who was also called John

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: a colorful, relatively hard form of limestone which may be polished to a lustrous finish (especially valued as material for building or for sculpture)
s.c: Where there is no technical term for ‘marble,’ one may use an expression such as ‘beautiful rock’ or ‘valuable stone.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: to provide information about a person or an event concerning which the speaker has direct knowledge{N:001}
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to indicate specifically what is the content of a witness, so that, for example, in ⟦Luke 21:13|Luke 21:13⟧ it may be necessary to say ‘this is your chance to witness to the good news’ or ‘… to tell about the good news’ or ‘… to tell what you yourselves know about the good news.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: to speak well of a person on the basis of personal experience
s.g: to speak well of; to approve of
s.c: It is possible that μαρτυρέω in ⟦Luke 4:22|Luke 4:22⟧ should be translated as ‘they were well impressed.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: to provide information about a person or an event concerning which the speaker has direct knowledge
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to indicate specifically what is the content of a witness, so that, for example, in ⟦Luke 21:13|Luke 21:13⟧ it may be necessary to say ‘this is your chance to witness to the good news’ or ‘… to tell about the good news’ or ‘… to tell what you yourselves know about the good news.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: (derivative of {L:μαρτυρέω<SDBG:μαρτυρέω:000000>}[a] ‘to witness,’ {D:33.262}) the content of what is witnessed or said
s.c: In a number of languages one must specify the content of the witness, and it also may be necessary to indicate the agent who is engaged in the witnessing. For example, in ⟦Mark 14:55|Mark 14:55⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘they tried to find someone who would testify against Jesus’ or ‘… say something against Jesus.’ In ⟦1 Corinthians 1:6|1 Corinthians 1:6⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘what we told you from personal experience about Christ has become so firmly fixed in you’ or ‘… has become so much a part of you.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: (derivative of {L:μαρτυρέω<SDBG:μαρτυρέω:000001>}[b] to speak well of, {D:33.263}) that which is said about a person on the basis of an evaluation of the persons conduct
s.c: In obtaining a satisfactory equivalent for ‘reputation,’ it may be necessary to restructure considerably the clause in which a term such as μαρτυρία or ὄνομα occurs. For example, in ⟦1 Timothy 3:7|1 Timothy 3:7⟧ one may translate ‘he should be the kind of man that people outside the church say is a good person.’ Similarly, in ⟦Revelation 3:1|Revelation 3:1⟧ one may need to translate ‘people speak of you as being alive even though you are dead.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: to provide information about a person or an event concerning which the speaker has direct knowledge
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to indicate specifically what is the content of a witness, so that, for example, in ⟦Luke 21:13|Luke 21:13⟧ it may be necessary to say ‘this is your chance to witness to the good news’ or ‘… to tell about the good news’ or ‘… to tell what you yourselves know about the good news.’

s.dp: Communication › Witness, Testify
s.d: (derivative of {L:μαρτυρέω<SDBG:μαρτυρέω:000000>}[a] ‘to witness,’ {D:33.262}) the content of what is witnessed or said
s.c: In a number of languages one must specify the content of the witness, and it also may be necessary to indicate the agent who is engaged in the witnessing. For example, in ⟦Mark 14:55|Mark 14:55⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘they tried to find someone who would testify against Jesus’ or ‘… say something against Jesus.’ In ⟦1 Corinthians 1:6|1 Corinthians 1:6⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘what we told you from personal experience about Christ has become so firmly fixed in you’ or ‘… has become so much a part of you.’

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: a person who has been deprived of life as the result of bearing witness to his beliefs
s.c: A strictly literal translation of the Greek expression in ⟦Revelation 17:6|Revelation 17:6⟧ (ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ ‘of the blood of the martyrs of Jesus’) is likely to result in considerable misunderstanding, for it could mean that these were individuals who had been martyred by Jesus rather than those who had been deprived of their lives because of their relationship to Jesus. It would be possible to render τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ as ‘those who had been killed because they belonged to Jesus,’ but one should avoid any expression which would suggest slave ownership.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Processes Involving the Mouth, Other Than Eating and Drinking
s.d: to bite with the teeth
s.c: In some languages it is important to distinguish clearly between three different kinds of biting: the biting of food, the biting of one’s own lips or tongue, and the biting of a person in a fight or quarrel.

s.dp: Physical Impact › Hit, Strike
s.d: to beat severely with a whip
s.g: to whip; to beat with a whip; whipping; flogging

s.dp: Punish, Reward › Punish

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: a state of disease, often implying divine punishment
s.g: to be diseased; to be sick; disease

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: the breast of both humans and animals, with special reference to the mammary glands
s.c: In ⟦Revelation 1:13|Revelation 1:13⟧ the phrase πρὸς τοῖς μαστοῖς is a reference to the particular location of the gold band which went around the chest and not to the mammary glands as such. In some languages, therefore, it is often preferable to use a phrase such as ‘around his chest’ rather than trying to be more specific, for example, ‘a gold band around his chest at the location of his breasts.’|In translating ⟦Luke 11:27|Luke 11:27⟧ it is important to use an expression which will be perfectly natural, for example, ‘the breasts that gave you milk’ or ‘the breasts from which you obtained milk.’ In some instances, however, a specific reference to breasts as the source of milk may seem somewhat vulgar, and therefore it may be better to speak of ‘happy is your mother who nursed you.’

s.dp: Communication › Foolish Talk
s.d: talk which has no beneficial purpose and is thus idle and meaningless

s.dp: Communication › Foolish Talk
s.d: (derivative of ματαιολογέω ‘to engage in idle talk,’ not occurring in the NT) one who engages in empty and idle talk

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: pertaining to being useless on the basis of being futile and lacking in content

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: pertaining to being useless on the basis of being futile and lacking in content

s.dp: Value › Useful, Useless
s.d: to become useless and hence worthless
s.g: to become futile; to become worthless; to become nonsense

s.dp: Relations › Result
s.d: pertaining to being without any result
s.g: in vain; to no avail; with no result

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the son of Semein in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Artifacts › Weapons and Armor
s.d: a relatively short sword (or even dagger) used for cutting and stabbing
s.c: The phrase στόμα μαχαίρης (literally ‘mouth of the sword’) refers to the event of killing or slaughter: ἔφυγον στόματα μαχαίρης ‘they escaped being killed by the sword’ ⟦Hebrews 11:34|Hebrews 11:34⟧. See LN 79.109.

s.dp: Military Activities › To Fight
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:μάχαιρα<SDBG:μάχαιρα:000000>}[a] ‘sword,’ {D:6.33})
s.c: For another interpretation of μάχαιρα in ⟦Matthew 10:34|Matthew 10:34⟧, see LN 39.25.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:μάχαιρα<SDBG:μάχαιρα:000000>}[a] ‘sword,’ {D:6.33}) death by violence or execution

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Strife, Struggle
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:μάχαιρα<SDBG:μάχαιρα:000000>}[a] ‘sword,’ {D:6.33}) a state of discord and strife
s.c: For another interpretation of μάχαιρα in ⟦Matthew 10:34|Matthew 10:34⟧, see LN 55.6.

s.dp: Punish, Reward › Punish
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to bear the sword) to have the capacity or authority to punish
s.g: to have the power to punish

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Strife, Struggle
s.d: serious conflict, either physical or non-physical, but clearly intensive and bitter
s.c: In order to suggest something of the intensity of conflict in μάχομαι and μάχη, it may be useful in some instances to employ similes in the rendering of these terms, for example, ‘they opposed one another just as though they were actually fighting one another’ or ‘they are fighting, as it were.’

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Strife, Struggle
s.d: serious conflict, either physical or non-physical, but clearly intensive and bitter
s.c: In order to suggest something of the intensity of conflict in μάχομαι and μάχη, it may be useful in some instances to employ similes in the rendering of these terms, for example, ‘they opposed one another just as though they were actually fighting one another’ or ‘they are fighting, as it were.’

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: a deed of importance and power
s.c: In some contexts it is not possible to distinguish readily between τέρας (LN 76.7), δύναμις (LN 76.7), and μεγαλεῖον, for all may refer to miraculous events, and in a number of instances these terms are used in pairs, primarily to emphasize rather than to distinguish different kinds of miraculous events. All of these expressions may indicate a supernatural component with important religious implications, especially since the performance of such miracles implies divine power.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a state of greatness or importance

s.dp: Power, Force
s.d: a manifestation of great power

s.dp: Features of Objects › Beautiful, Ugly
s.d: pertaining to being unusually attractive and beautiful
s.c: For μεγαλοπρεπής as part of a title, see LN 12.6.

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: a title for God, literally: majestic glory
s.c: It is rare that one can use a literal rendering of μεγαλοπρεπὴς δόξα as a title for God, since ‘Sublime Glory’ is a quality and not normally a reference to a person or supernatural being.|It is also possible, however, to use a descriptive phrase such as ‘the one who is supremely glorious’ or ‘the one who is glorious above all others’ or ‘God who is supremely glorious.’ See LN 79.14.

s.dp: Features of Objects › Large, Small
s.d: to cause to be large
s.g: to make big; to make large; to enlarge
s.c: It is possible to interpret the large size of the tassels as referring primarily to the length of the tassels and, therefore, to translate as ‘they make their tassels long.’ However, it seems more likely that the reference includes all dimensions.

s.dp: Communication › Praise
s.d: to praise a person in terms of that individuals greatness
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to restructure a statement such as ‘praising God’s greatness’ as a form of direct discourse, for example, ‘they said, God is indeed great.’

s.dp: Status › Honor or Respect in Relation to Status
s.d: to show respect to a person on the basis of the importance of such an individual
s.g: to pay special respect to; to hold in high honor; to regard as important

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: the upper range of a scale of extent, with the possible implication of importance in relevant contexts
s.g: great; greatly; greatness; to a great degree; intense; terrible
s.c: In a number of languages the expression of intense degree associated with some activity or state is expressed by means of a verb, not an adverb, so that one may render ⟦Philippians 4:10|Philippians 4:10⟧ literally as ‘I am-intense joyous in the Lord,’ in which the form ‘am-intense’ is an attempt to represent a verb expression in such a language.

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a state of greatness or importance

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a title for God, literally: majesty) one who is characterized by majesty and greatness
s.c: The use of ‘Majesty’ as a title for God may be rendered in some languages as ‘the one who is truly great’ or ‘… truly important.’ In other instances a more satisfactory equivalent is ‘the one who is truly wonderful.’

s.dp: Quantity › Much, Little [Masses, Collectives, Extensions]
s.d: a large quantity, involving extent

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: the upper range of a scale of extent, with the possible implication of importance in relevant contexts
s.g: great; greatly; greatness; to a great degree; intense; terrible

s.dp: Features of Objects › Large, Small
s.d: a large size, relative to the norm for the class of objects in question

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: pertaining to being great in terms of status

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Surprise, Astonish
s.d: pertaining to being surprising in view of being important

s.dp: Degree › More Than, Less Than [Comparative Degree]
s.d: a degree which surpasses in some manner a point on an explicit or implicit scale of extent{N:001}
s.g: more; more than; to a greater degree; even more

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: pertaining to having a higher status in comparison to something else

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to the older of two objects
s.c: In some languages ‘the older will serve the younger’ must be rendered as ‘the one who was born first will serve the one who was born later.’

s.dp: Value › Important, Unimportant
s.d: pertaining to being extremely important

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a relatively long duration of time
s.g: long; long time; for some time

s.dp: Status
s.d: persons of important or high status

s.dp: Degree › Much, Little [Positive-Negative Degree]
s.d: the upper range of a scale of extent, with the possible implication of importance in relevant contexts
s.g: great; greatly; greatness; to a great degree; intense; terrible
s.c: In ⟦Ephesians 1:19|Ephesians 1:19⟧ there are two expressions of degree, ὑπερβάλλον (treated in LN 78.33) and μέγεθος, which, though syntactically the head of the phrase, is semantically an expression of degree with δύναμις ‘power’ (LN 76.1).

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a person of particularly great importance and high status

s.dp: Communication › Interpret, Mean, Explain
s.d: to translate from one language to another
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to translate’ or ‘to interpret’ is an idiomatic expression, for example, ‘it comes out in our language as’ or ‘in our words it means’ or ‘in our mouths it says.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Drunkenness
s.d: to become drunk on alcoholic beverages

s.dp: Linear Movement › Move, Come/Go
s.d: to cause something to be moved from one place to another
s.g: to cause to move; to remove
s.c: It is not possible to determine whether in ⟦1 Corinthians 13:2|1 Corinthians 13:2⟧ one should understand ‘remove mountains’ in the sense of ‘causing them to disappear’ or ‘to cause a mountain to change its location,’ that is to say, to move a mountain from one place to another.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: to cause a change of state, with emphasis upon the difference in the resulting state{N:001}
s.g: to change to; to turn into; to cause to be different from; to transform

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:μεθίστημι<SDBG:μεθίστημι:000000>}[a] ‘to cause to move,’ {D:15.9}) to cause a complete change in someone’s beliefs, normally in the unfavorable sense of causing someone to turn away from a previous belief and hence to be misled

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: to cease from a state or function, with the implication of transfer or removal
s.c: See also μεθίστημι in LN 13.64.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Mislead, Lead Astray, Deceive
s.d: crafty scheming with the intent to deceive

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Drunkenness
s.d: to become intoxicated

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Drunkenness
s.d: a person who habitually drinks too much and thus becomes a drunkard

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Drunkenness
s.d: to become drunk on alcoholic beverages

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to drink wine or beer (distilled alcoholic beverages were not known in the ancient world), usually with emphasis upon drinking relatively large quantities
s.g: to drink freely; to drink a great deal; to get drunk

s.dp: Features of Objects › Color
s.c: Expressions for a number of terms for color differ on the basis of the object which is designated as having such a color. For example, a term for black as applied to a horse may be a different term from what one would use in speaking of a black box.

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
s.d: a dark liquid used in writing or marking
s.c: The use of ink is so universal at the present time that some term or expression for it is almost inevitable in all languages. However, in some cases the equivalent is essentially a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘black stain’ or ‘writing stain.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to think about something in such a way as to make an appropriate response
s.g: to think about; to be concerned about
s.c: It may be possible to render ‘is God concerned about oxen’ (⟦1 Corinthians 9:9|1 Corinthians 9:9⟧) as ‘is God thinking about doing something about oxen.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: to be particularly concerned about something, with the implication of some apprehension
s.g: to be of concern; to be anxious about
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to be concerned about’ may be simply ‘to think about,’ and the negative might be merely ‘not to let something enter one’s head.’

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to keep on giving serious consideration to something
s.g: to ponder; to let one’s mind dwell on; to keep thinking about; to fix one’s attention on
s.c: It is also possible to understand μελετάω in ⟦1 Timothy 4:15|1 Timothy 4:15⟧ as meaning ‘to do’ or ‘to practice,’ as noted in LN 68.20.

s.dp: Think › To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
s.d: to think seriously about a particular course of action
s.g: to plan to act; to plot

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: to continue to perform certain activities with care and concern
s.g: to practice; to continue to do; to cultivate
s.c: The construction in ⟦1 Timothy 4:15|1 Timothy 4:15⟧, in which ταῦτα μελέτα and ἐν τούτοις ἴσθι appear to be essentially synonymous reinforcements one of the other, would appear to fully justify combining these expressions as essentially equivalent in meaning, but for another interpretation of μελετάω in ⟦1 Timothy 4:15|1 Timothy 4:15⟧, see LN 30.20.

s.dp: Foods and Condiments › Food
s.d: a sweet substance produced by bees from flower nectar
s.c: Though honey may be regarded by some as a vegetable product, since flowers constitute its source, it is more specifically associated with bees and in some languages is actually called bee urine.|μέλι ἄγριον, literally ‘wild honey,’ refers to bee honey gathered in the fields and not the result of keeping bees in hives.|In the ancient world bee keeping was a highly developed industry, since honey was a principal source of sweetening. The equivalent of wild honey in a number of languages is ‘forest honey’ or ‘tree honey.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: an island located south of Sicily

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: to occur at a point of time in the future which is subsequent to another event and closely related to it

s.dp: Mode › Necessary, Unnecessary
s.d: to be inevitable, with respect to future developments
s.c: In a number of languages there is a problem involved in speaking of what is necessary or inevitable in the future, for a distinction is made between that which is purely impersonal or physical and that which is the result of some person’s purpose, intent, or activity. As in the case of δεῖ in ⟦Mark 13:7|Mark 13:7⟧ (LN 71.34), it is impossible in the case of μέλλω in ⟦Matthew 17:12|Matthew 17:12⟧ to determine whether the reference is merely to an inevitable future event (‘bound to happen’) or whether this is part of the plan and purpose of God. In order to avoid a wrong interpretation of ⟦Matthew 17:12|Matthew 17:12⟧, it may therefore be useful to translate as ‘in the same way the Son of Man will most certainly be mistreated by them.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: to extend time unduly, with the implication of lack of decision

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: unlimited extent of time beginning with the time of the discourse

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: a part of the body{N:001}
s.c: In some languages an equivalent of μέλος is simply ‘division,’ and in a few languages an even more generic expression such as ‘things’ is used, so that ‘the parts of the body’ may be rendered by an expression meaning literally ‘things of the body.’|In different languages the various parts of the body are classified in a number of diverse ways. In some languages the sensory organs of seeing, hearing, smelling, and tasting (those related to the head) are often set off from other types of organs, while in other languages special terms may be employed for those organs involving movement, for example, the joints, arms, legs, etc. Other languages make extensive subclassifications of body parts on the basis of whether they are external or internal, though such classifications often appear to be arbitrary, since teeth and tongue may be regarded as either external or internal.

s.dp: Whole, Unite, Part, Divide › Part
s.d: a part as a member of a unit
s.g: member (based on the figure of the relationship of parts to the body)

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Λευί[c] in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Neri in the genealogy of Jesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Aminadam in the genealogy of Jesus ({S:04200303300000}, apparatus)

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a king of Salem and priest of the Most High God in the time of Abraham

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus
